input: Rewire the outdoor patio string lights safely

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a full rewire from scratch, replacing a damaged section, or just re-routing existing wiring changes the entire plan and materials needed.
Whether the user is doing this themselves or hiring an electrician determines how technical and safety-focused the guidance needs to be.
The power source type (standard outlet, hardwired circuit, solar, low-voltage transformer) fundamentally changes the wiring approach and safety requirements.
Local electrical codes, permits, or HOA rules may restrict what can be done DIY, what materials are required, and how the work must be completed.
The mounting setup (hung between posts, draped along a fence, stapled to a structure) affects what hardware, wire gauge, and weatherproofing solutions are needed.
Whether the priority is aesthetics, durability, cost savings, or code compliance shapes which materials and methods to recommend.
Knowing what went wrong with the current setup (flickering, broken socket, frayed wire, full failure) clarifies what a successful outcome looks like and what to avoid repeating.

gold.taskTitle: Rewire outdoor patio string lights safely
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to safely rewire their outdoor patio string lights, which involves electrical work in an exterior environment.

questions.title: What part of the lights actually needs rewiring?
questions.description: Is this a full rewire from scratch, replacing a damaged section of wire, fixing specific sockets, or re-routing the existing strand to a new path?

questions.title: Are you doing this yourself or hiring someone?
questions.description: Determines how technical the guidance should be — full DIY step-by-step with safety warnings vs. what to brief a hired electrician on.

questions.title: What is the power source for these lights?
questions.description: Standard outdoor outlet, hardwired into a circuit, low-voltage transformer, or solar — each has very different wiring requirements and safety considerations.

questions.title: How are the lights currently mounted or hung?
questions.description: Strung between posts, draped along a fence, stapled to a pergola, etc. — the mounting method determines hardware, wire support, and weatherproofing needs.

questions.title: Do local codes or permits apply to this project?
questions.description: Some jurisdictions require permits or licensed electricians for outdoor wiring work; knowing this prevents doing work that must later be redone or inspected.

questions.title: What matters most to you — durability, looks, or cost?
questions.description: Shapes the choice of wire type, connectors, and weatherproofing — e.g., heavy-duty outdoor-rated wire vs. a budget solution that still meets safety minimums.

questions.title: What problem with the current lights prompted this rewire?
questions.description: Flickering, a broken socket, frayed or damaged wire, or complete failure — the root cause defines what a successful fix looks like and what to avoid repeating.
